The Imperial Iranian Army was one of the most important institutions of the Iranian state during the Pahlavi era (1925–1979). It played a central role in protecting the country’s territorial integrity, maintaining national security, strengthening the authority of the central government, and establishing Iran as a major regional power. Throughout this period, the Iranian  military underwent significant transformations in its organization, equipment, training, and strategic capabilities. These developments were particularly noticeable during the reign of Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi, when Iran invested enormous financial resources in modernizing its armed forces. By the late 1970s, Iran possessed one of the most powerful and technologically advanced  militaries in the Middle East.

The creation of a modern Iranian army began under Reza Shah Pahlavi, who recognized that a strong and centralized military was essential for establishing a stable and independent nation. Before his rise to power, during the Qajar dynasty, Iran lacked a unified military organization capable of effectively defending the country’s borders and maintaining security throughout its territory. The armed forces were fragmented, poorly equipped, and frequently dependent on tribal forces and foreign military assistance. This situation weakened the central government and made Iran vulnerable to foreign interference, particularly from Russia and Britain. Reza Shah therefore considered military reform one of the most important priorities of his government.
